target.installProfile: Recommended default (README.md:169-221): npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup -> ecc@ecc Claude Code plugin, Global user scope, Standard hook profile. Rules are not installed (plugins cannot distribute them, README.md:298-308). Primary harness: Claude Code.

evidence: agents/code-reviewer.md:27-33 — clear: 'Only report issues you are confident about (>80% sure it is a real problem)'

rules/common/agents.md:38 — weak: 'ALWAYS use parallel Task execution for independent operations' (absolute, no scope); agents/code-reviewer.md:3 'MUST BE USED for all code changes' while 22 other *-reviewer agents exist with no rule saying which wins

Cross-checked, no contradiction: 80% coverage (rules/common/testing.md:3, development-workflow.md:28, code-review.md:37/80, agents/tdd-guide.md:3, skills/tdd-workflow/SKILL.md:3); counts 68/293/94 (.claude-plugin/plugin.json, README.md:142-148, AGENTS.md:3; README.md:1699 is the v2.0.0 changelog); SessionStart cap 8000 chars (README.md:1339 vs scripts/hooks/session-start.js:41)

scores.missingForNext: Reasons for the mandatory workflow rules (coverage floor, TDD for all types, review on every change).
evidence: Sample: the first ALWAYS/NEVER/MANDATORY rule of each of rules/common/{coding-style,agents,testing,code-review,development-workflow,security}.md plus the hooks that block (config-protection, gateguard) and the next unexplained rule in agents.md, testing.md and security.md — 10 rules, 4 with a specific reason

With reason: rules/common/coding-style.md:5-12 immutability ('prevents hidden side effects'); rules/common/agents.md:55 final message is the deliverable (children cannot notify a parent whose turn ended); scripts/hooks/config-protection.js:5-7 (agents weaken configs instead of fixing code); scripts/hooks/gateguard-fact-force.js:5-9 ('are you sure?' is always answered yes)

Without reason: rules/common/testing.md:3 80% coverage; testing.md:5 all three test types required; code-review.md:9 mandatory review after any change; development-workflow.md:9 research mandatory before any implementation; agents.md:38 always parallel; security.md:18 always env vars

scores.missingForNext: A risk scale whose tiers change what is required, with an explicit skip at low risk.
evidence: No change-risk scale. rules/common/testing.md:12-18 'MANDATORY workflow' and :5 'Test Types (ALL required)'; rules/common/code-review.md:9-15 mandatory review after writing or modifying any code; agents/code-reviewer.md:3 'MUST BE USED for all code changes'

The only tiering is finding severity (rules/common/code-review.md:55 CRITICAL -> BLOCK) and one trigger for security-sensitive code (:13); neither changes what a low-risk change may skip. No 'trivial'/'typo' exception found in rules/common/*.md

penalties.why: ECC_HOOKS_ENABLED=false or the plugin option hooks_enabled / ecc/setup.json (scripts/lib/hook-flags.js:64-73) turns every hook off, block-no-verify included; settings.json, where both live, is not gated
ECC_HOOK_PROFILE=minimal or the plugin option hook_profile (scripts/lib/hook-flags.js:75-84) drops gateguard and config-protection, which run only on standard,strict (hooks/hooks.json)
ECC_DISABLED_HOOKS=<ids> (scripts/lib/hook-flags.js:86-97) disables any hook by id, including pre:bash:block-no-verify
ECC_GATEGUARD=off or GATEGUARD_DISABLED=1 (scripts/hooks/gateguard-fact-force.js:1321-1325); the deny message itself tells the model to use it (:1759, :1798)
GATEGUARD_EXEMPT_GLOBS (scripts/hooks/gateguard-fact-force.js:110-162) exempts any path from the edit gate

evidence: Profile read: standard (default per scripts/lib/hook-flags.js:82 and README.md:1333-1334). Hook ids and profiles from the commands in hooks/hooks.json.

E1 absent — the only write-time secret scan is pre-bash-commit-quality.js:132-158, which blocks a commit (exit 2, :502-503) but is registered for the strict profile only (scripts/hooks/bash-hook-dispatcher.js:43-44). governance-capture records, it does not block, and is opt-in (hooks.metadata.json, ECC_GOVERNANCE_CAPTURE=1). No Write/Edit content check found.

E2 block — scripts/hooks/block-no-verify.js:123-158, :229-241, exit 2 at :759/:785, on minimal,standard,strict (bash-hook-dispatcher.js:24-25). Covers --no-verify, commit -n in clusters, -c core.hooksPath. Gaps: --no-gpg-sign is not checked; the PowerShell matcher runs only gateguard (hooks/hooks.json), so the PowerShell tool is not covered.

E3 warn — ECC declares no high-risk paths. config-protection.js:1-60 blocks edits to a fixed list of linter/formatter configs. gateguard-fact-force.js denies the first Edit/Write of every file and asks the model for facts, then allows the retry (:1730-1800): the model clears it, the user is never asked. Scored warn, not confirm.

E4 absent — Bash/PowerShell gateguard gates destructive commands (rm, destructive git, dd, SQL: gateguard-fact-force.js:794-805) and quotes the instruction once per session for routine ones; a redirect into a source file is routine.

E5 absent — gateguard exempts .claude/settings*.json explicitly (gateguard-fact-force.js:1621-1624, :1865, :1898); config-protection's list has no ECC or Claude hook config; the plugin's hooks.json lives in the plugin cache with no gate.

Checklist 0+2+1+0+0 = 3; five ungated off-switches (-10); clamped to 0, which matches anchor 0 ('every blocking hook can be turned off by an ungated switch'). Advisory-labeled-enforced was not searched exhaustively: the score is already at the floor.

notes: First run of this target under rubric 1.0.0; no previous run, so no deltas. Context cost counts the descriptions the plugin installs. Claude Code caps the skill listing (third-party sources put the cap at 1-2% of the context window; not verified against official docs), so part of ECC's 14201 skill and command words may never reach the model, at the price of those skills not auto-invoking. The rubric's method does not say whether a harness cap is subtracted; this run did not subtract it. Audited from source at the tag, not from an installed plugin; the default profile was read from README.md and hooks/hooks.json. The auditor ran under canonkit's rules, not ECC's.
